questions.stem:

immediate neighbor of C. R sits second to the left of Q. Q does not sit at the end of the row. B sits second
to the right of A. The one who faces B sits immediate right of P . S sits exactly between Q and U.

"Only violin are drums" gives drums ⊆ violin. Neither salad nor pasta is explicitly excluded from drums. Thus some drums being salad is possible under ordinary subset logic, while no salad being drums is not forced. The PDF's key assumes an additional exclusivity convention.

Two inlet pipes A and B and one outlet pipe C connected to a tank. In a minute, part of tank filled
by pipes A and C together is 30% that of filled by pipes B and C together. Find the time taken by pipe A
alone to fill the tank?
Statement I: Time taken by pipe B alone to fill the tank is 5 minutes.
Statement II: Ratio of efficiency of pipe A to pipe C is 5: 2.
The following questions are accompany by two statements i. e. statement (I) and statement (II). You
have to determine which statement (s) is/are sufficient/necessary to answer the questions.
options: Neither statement I nor statement II alone is sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not sufficient.
Either statement I or statement II alone is sufficient.
Both statements together are necessary; neither statement alone is sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not sufficient.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (d) Both statements together are necessary; neither statement alone is sufficient.

Let A, B and C denote the positive fill/fill/drain rates. The given relation is A − C = 0.3(B − C). Statement I gives B = 1/5 but leaves A and C undetermined. Statement II gives A = 2.5C but no absolute rate. Together: 1.5C = 0.3(1/5 − C), so C = 1/30 and A = 1/12. A fills the tank in 12 minutes. Both statements are needed.
